text:
Help me write a public comment. I run a charter fishing boat out of our harbor, and the state fish and wildlife commission is taking comment on cutting the daily summer flounder limit from 4 fish per angler to 2.

Facts:
- I've run my boat for 22 years. I take out about 160 trips a season at $900 a trip for up to 6 people.
- There are 11 charter boats in our harbor.
- In a survey our charter association ran, 41 of 70 past customers said they would book fewer trips if the limit drops to 2. 12 said they'd book the same number.
- The commission staff's report says the flounder stock is at 78% of its target and recommends the cut for 3 years.
- Charter boats land about 9% of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80%.
- The last time the limit was cut, in 2016, my bookings dropped from 170 trips to 138 the next season and came back to 155 two years later.

I want to say this limit will put every charter boat in our harbor out of business. I get two minutes at the microphone.

Before I draft, one thing you should know: your own numbers don't back up "every charter boat will go out of business." In 2016 your bookings fell 19% and came back to 155 within two years. The commission staff may well know that history. If you open with a claim they can disprove, they may stop listening to the rest of your two minutes. Your strongest case is that the cut hits charters hard while charters land only 9% of the fish. That case gets stronger if you can show what lost trips actually cost.

These answers would change what I write:

1. **What do you want the commission to do instead?** For example: keep 4, settle on 3, give charter boats a separate limit, make the cut shorter than 3 years, or use a size limit or season change instead. Asking for something specific usually lands better than a flat no.
2. **How many trips can you lose before you stop making money?** What does a season cost you to run (fuel, slip, insurance, crew, boat payments)? If you went from 160 trips to 130 and that wipes out your profit, that's what makes "out of business" believable.
3. **What happened to the other boats after 2016?** Did any of the 11 (or the boats there then) close, sell, or cut back? Did the bounce back to 155 happen for other reasons, like the limit going back up or prices rising?
4. **More on the survey:** what did the other 17 of the 70 say? Did anyone say how many fewer trips they'd book? How were the 70 picked? The commission will ask whether it's a fair sample.
5. **Who else depends on these trips?** For example, deckhands, tackle shops, marinas, motels and restaurants. Rough numbers are fine.
6. **For the opening line:** what's your name, your boat's name, the harbor, and do you speak for the charter association or just yourself?

And one open question: is there anything else the commission knows or will find out that cuts against you? For example, charter landings going over a past target, catches already dropping, or the association backing an earlier cut.

If you don't know some of these, tell me and I'll write without them.

1. We'd accept 3 fish or a shorter season instead of 2. I can also commit to giving commission staff my trip logs from 2016 on, and our charter association can commit to testing a catch-reporting app with the staff next season.

2. I don't know. I haven't worked that out.

3. I don't know what happened to the other boats after 2016, or why my bookings came back. Two other captains in our harbor have told me they'd sell if bookings drop like they did in 2016. I can't say how many boats would close. I only know my own books.

4. I don't know.

5. I don't know.

6. Captain Ray Dunn, the Sea Lark. I don't know if I'm speaking for the association.

Open question: I don't dispute the staff's stock numbers, and I don't have an answer to them. Also, about 70% of my trips for this season are already booked.

I hear you on "every boat will go out of business." Make it as strong as you can, but in words that aren't false.

I wrote it to run about 270 words, which is roughly two minutes at a steady pace. Read it aloud once with a timer and cut a sentence if you run over.

<final_document>
Good evening. I'm Captain Ray Dunn. I've run the Sea Lark out of [harbor name] for 22 years, about 160 trips a season.

I'm not here to argue with your staff's numbers. The stock is at 78 percent of target, and it needs to rebuild. I'm asking you to rebuild it in a way that doesn't hit hardest the boats that take the smallest share.

Charter boats land about 9 percent of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80 percent. But our customers pay for a day of fishing, and what they can take home is a big part of what they're paying for.

I've been through this before. After the 2016 cut, my bookings fell from 170 trips to 138 the next season. That's 32 trips, close to 29,000 dollars, on one boat. Two years later I was back to 155, still short of where I started.

This time our charter association asked 70 past customers. Forty-one said they'd book fewer trips at two fish. Only 12 said they'd book the same.

There are 11 charter boats in our harbor. Two other captains have told me that if bookings drop like they did in 2016, they'll sell. I can't tell you how many boats would close. I can tell you some of us are that close to the edge.

So here's what I'm asking. Set the limit at three fish, or shorten the season instead of cutting to two.

And here's what I'll offer. My trip logs from 2016 to today, open to your staff. And our association is ready to test a catch-reporting app with your staff next season, so you'll have better charter data than you have now.

Thank you.
</final_document>

Some notes:

- **"Out of business":** I didn't use that phrase. Instead the speech says two captains told you they'd sell, that you can't say how many boats would close, and that some of you are "that close to the edge." Everything there is true. Admitting what you don't know should also make the rest easier to believe.
- **The association:** you told me they can commit to testing the app, but you're not sure you speak for them. Check with them before the hearing. If you can't, change that line to "our association has told me it's willing to..."
- **The $29,000:** that's 32 lost trips × $900. It's money from bookings, not profit, so the speech calls it bookings.
- **I left out that 70% of next season is already booked.** It could sound like demand is strong no matter what the limit is. If the commission asks, you can honestly say those customers booked expecting four fish.
- **For your Q&A:** if you can work out how many trips a season you need to break even, that's the number most likely to change minds. It's also the honest way to back up "close to the edge."
